I think I'm more in favor of this one, since it would more closely match the behavior of sending meta results through the queue.

I'm still not in love with the tests.  It's testing afinity by looking at the output, and just assuming it reflects what is actually happening.  It's a few steps too far removed from what the actual issue is, but I don't know of a better way.  I suppose a custom callback could help, but then I also wonder if it worth the trouble. I agree. I tried and implemented the custom callback approach, it wasn't much effort to get that done. I changed the testing playbook a bit to force which tasks are the first and last in the play so we know hosts started executing as soon as possible. I think the test is still fragile in that it makes assumptions based on the code internals and the callback is tightly coupled with the testing playbook but there shouldn't be a reason to touch it hopefully. And if we go ahead and make the meta tasks results go through the results queue we can probably just get rid of the test.

issue_context.title: `meta` tasks break host/fork affinity with `host_pinned` strategy
issue_context.body:
### Summary

When using the `host_pinned` strategy, any `meta` task that executes can cause the plugin to lose the ability to track host/fork affinity.  This ultimately affects any use of roles in a play using the `host_pinned` strategy.

In essence, `host_pinned` is meant to work like `free` + `serial: N`, where `N` would be the number of forks with `host_pinned`.  Supplying `serial: N` on the play with `host_pinned` will additionally address the issue as a work around.

The cause is due to `meta` tasks not being real tasks, and bypassing many of the logic in the strategy. As such, we don't properly mark a host as "blocked" or track that we have spawned more tasks than should be queued.  This results in extra tasks being queued or direct execution of `meta` tasks, outside the bounds of the fork limit.  An important note is that the fork count is still limited, and only `N` number of host/task are executed in parallel at any time.  The outcome is that the `host_pinned` strategy effectively turns into `free`.

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

lib/ansible/plugins/strategy/host_pinned.py

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version

  config file = /Users/sivel/projects/ansibledev/playbooks/host_pinned/ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/Users/sivel/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /Users/sivel/projects/ansibledev/ansible/lib/ansible
  ansible collection location = /Users/sivel/.ansible/collections:/usr/share/ansible/collections
  executable location = /Users/sivel/projects/ansibledev/ansible/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.11.2 (main, Mar  2 2023, 12:04:14) [Clang 14.0.0 (clang-1400.0.29.202)] (/Users/sivel/venvs/ansibledev/bin/python)
  jinja version = 3.1.3
  libyaml = True
```


### Configuration

```console
# if using a version older than ansible-core 2.12 you should omit the '-t all'
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed -t all
```


### OS / Environment

N/A

### Steps to Reproduce

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
```
├── ansible.cfg
│   │ [defaults]
│   │ forks = 2
│   │ inventory = hosts
├── hosts
│   │ localhost0
│   │ localhost1
│   │ localhost2
│   │ localhost3
│   │ localhost4
│   │ localhost5
│   │ localhost6
│   │ localhost7
│   │ localhost8
│   │ localhost9
│   │
│   │ [all:vars]
│   │ ansible_connection=local
│   │ ansible_python_interpreter={{ansible_playbook_python}}
├── playbook.yml
│   │ - hosts: all
│   │   gather_facts: false
│   │   strategy: host_pinned
│   │   tasks:
│   │     - name: start
│   │       debug:
│   │         msg: start
│   │
│   │     - ping:
│   │
│   │     - meta: noop
│   │
│   │     - debug:
│   │         msg: end
```


### Expected Results

host/fork affinity to be maintained

### Actual Results

```console
host/fork affinity is lost
```

review_comments: Just to make sure this is a little less likely to be affected by changes elsewhere, could we also add a `display` here too?  And ensure we don't see the output. Just concerned that if something happens to how we catch exceptions, this could be swallowed, and then we'd have the potential to see false positives.
